takeaways: Beat on both lines: diluted EPS of $3.16 vs $2.85 expected, and revenue of $4.87 billion, up 19%, vs $4.75 billion (Investing.com). Airbnb called it its fastest revenue growth in more than three years.
Bookings are hot: gross booking value rose 21% to $27.7 billion, nights and seats booked grew 16% to 155 million, and average daily rates rose 4% to $179 (company / Investing.com).
Profits followed: net income jumped 38% to $1.89 billion, and adjusted EBITDA rose 22% to $2.51 billion with a 52% margin.

It raised the full-year outlook to high-teens revenue growth and ~36% adjusted EBITDA margin, guided Q4 revenue to $3.22-$3.28 billion (above the ~$3.16 billion Street number), and authorized up to an additional $12 billion in Class A buybacks.
Investing.com's after-hours movers piece had ABNB up about 7% early; Yahoo Finance later showed roughly $188 vs a $170.13 regular-session close.
verdict: Airbnb just rediscovered the growth button it misplaced around 2023 and is acting like it never left. Beat, raise, $12 billion more buybacks, and an AI travel agent promised for 2027. After hours the stock woke up too — which is what happens when a $100 billion vacation marketplace remembers how to book nights.
